1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which derives the account exclusively from session.userId (never from client-supplied IDs), so MFA settings are bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Verification challenges are hashed and stored per-session (session.identity) and the system has only one account, so codes are not cross-user; only the default demo mode reuses the fixed code '123456' across sessions.

3.why: Nothing in the MFA-enablement path (authenticator/verify, backup/confirm) invalidates or rotates sessions—sessions.delete occurs only at sign-in and logout—so pre-existing sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted via encrypt() and recovery codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in account.backups.

5.why: Production generation uses crypto's randomBytes/randomInt (CSPRNG) for secrets, session IDs and codes, but the default demo mode substitutes hardcoded identity, authenticator and recovery codes.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used anywhere in the client, the session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and secrets/codes live only in in-memory page variables that are cleared on step change.

7.why: The server validates email (emailOK), OTPs (otpOK), recovery codes (codeOK), the delivery-method allowlist, password length and body size/type; storage is in-memory Maps so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent/replaceChildren (never innerHTML), the server templates no user data into the page, and a nonce-based CSP blocks any injected script execution.

9.why: The server issues no redirects whatsoever—navigation is same-page view switching—so there is no open-redirect surface and nothing outside an internal allow-list can occur.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY (plus Referrer/Permissions-Policy) on every response.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is set (and cleared) with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict attributes plus a Max-Age.

12.why: Server-side logging and error output are clean (generic 500 message, no stack traces, no secrets in URLs), but demo mode deliberately writes the identity, authenticator and recovery codes to the browser console log.

13.why: Identity codes carry used/expires flags with a 10-minute life, recovery codes are marked used on redemption, and TOTP codes are time-windowed with pendingSecret cleared after a successful verify.

14.why: failed()/isLocked() enforce 5-attempt/15-minute lockouts on sign-in, identity, authenticator and recovery verification, and identity-code requests are capped at 3 per 15 minutes.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID, getSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
